name: Popover
summary: A small floating panel on the native popover attribute, opened by a button with popovertarget and placed next to it.
description:
Use a popover for extra detail or a few controls tied to one button, which people can glance at and dismiss. It does not block the page; when the choice must be made first, use a dialog.

Where CSS anchor positioning exists it opens next to its trigger and flips when it runs out of room. Elsewhere vectra.js places it the same way (anchor.js runs by itself, no attribute needed).

classes.name: v-popover
classes.description: The panel, on an element with the popover attribute. Opens below its trigger, aligned to the start edge.

classes.name: v-popover-text
classes.description: Body text in the secondary colour.

classes.name: v-popover-top
classes.description: Prefers the space above the trigger.

classes.name: v-popover-start
classes.description: Opens beside the trigger on the start side.

classes.name: v-popover-end
classes.description: Opens beside the trigger on the end side.

states.description: Makes the element a popover: hidden until opened, then shown in the top layer. The default (auto) closes on Escape and on a click outside.
On the trigger button: the id of the popover it toggles. It also makes the trigger the anchor.
The open state, used by the CSS for the fade and scale.

keyboard.action: On the trigger, opens or closes the popover.
From the trigger, moves into the open popover, then on through the page.
Closes the popover and returns focus to the trigger if focus was inside.

a11y: Use a real <button> with popovertarget as the trigger, so the browser exposes the expanded state and handles focus.
The popover follows its trigger in the focus order, so keyboard users reach its content straight after the button.
Keep it to short content. Anything people must complete belongs in a dialog.

examples.title: Below and above
examples.description: Click a button to open its popover. Escape or a click outside closes it.
